requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version so standard system updates do not change it.
requirements.summary: curl began installed and unheld at 7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19, was placed on the native dpkg/APT hold, and remained at that version and held after restart. Final simulated upgrade and dist-upgrade operations both reported that curl would not be changed.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use an approach compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Ubuntu 16.04 with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic across the work and a full restart. The implementation used the platform-native apt-mark/dpkg hold mechanism and installed no replacement software.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. curl is held at 7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19, standard upgrade simulations leave it unchanged, and the hold persists through restart. Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic were retained. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for the sole managed node: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart identity changed, and system, package, and curl health recovered. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot transition and unchanged platform.
limitations: No real package upgrade was applied; update behavior was validated with apt-get simulated upgrade and dist-upgrade operations plus the persistent native hold. This is strong but non-destructive evidence rather than observation of a live update.
There is no separate cluster workload or application data in the stated single-node task to validate beyond system, package-manager, and curl recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: All potentially state-changing actions had clear roles: apt-mark hold curl established the requested protection (cmd-c183f2aabe104d03), and the scheduled reboot exercised the mandatory provider restart protocol (cmd-77d26a2ffb274683). The other commands were read-only checks, polling, or simulated upgrades. No unnecessary mutations were identified. Final evidence shows a clean package state, no failed services, no new listening sockets, and only normal reboot-generated systemd temporary-directory turnover.
